name: drugs in pregnancy and lactation overview
title: Whether a medicine is worth it in pregnancy or breastfeeding: in pregnancy most drugs are probably safe and the untreated disease is weighed against the drug, while a few major teratogens are switched or counselled on; in breastfeeding most drugs are safe if the relative infant dose is under 10 percent, a short list is contraindicated, and alcohol, tobacco, coffee and cannabis each have their own rule

root.title: A medicine in pregnancy or breastfeeding: is it worth it?
lines: most drugs reach the baby, and most are still safe · always weigh the risk of the UNTREATED disease
the risk depends on the drug, the dose, the timing, genetic susceptibility and her disease
> 90% of pregnant women take a medicine (2.9 on average) · < 10% of drugs (1980–2010) have fetal risk data · < 50% of pregnancies planned
counsel by context: BEFORE (planning) · DURING (taking it) · AFTER (a baby with a malformation) · unsure → FRAME clinic

groups.title: PREGNANT: the placenta is NOT a barrier
lines: preimplantation: ALL OR NONE (miscarriage) · embryonic (organogenesis): MAJOR malformations · fetal: FUNCTIONAL defects

groups.title: BREASTFEEDING: how much reaches the baby, and can the baby clear it?
lines: most drugs cross into milk, in minute amounts

head: h
Most drugs: probably safe
baseline major malformation risk 2–4%: 97% have a healthy baby
causes: genetic 25% · drugs 1% · unknown 50%
inv: A malformation is > 99 in 100 times NOT a drug
• put her risk in perspective: fear harms too
• animal data mislead: > 1200 drugs malformative in animals, not humans
tx: Treat: do NOT deny an effective drug
fewest drugs, as little as needed
fetal harm often found years after release

head: h
Major teratogen
even these harm only a fraction of exposed babies
clue: • alcohol · phenytoin, topiramate · methimazole · tetracycline, trimethoprim · misoprostol · lead, mercury
tx: counsel on timing and dose: see the ANTENATAL CARE chart

head: h
Usually SAFE
most medications are not contraindicated
clue: • high maternal blood level, fat-soluble or transported (BCRP)
• small: > 500 daltons stays out (insulin > 6000, heparin 40,000; ethanol 200 gets in)
• then must be absorbed from the baby's gut
inv: • milk concentration × 150 mL/kg/day ÷ maternal dose per kg per day
• milk/plasma ratio > 1 = concentrates in milk, but often harmless
2 · Can the baby absorb and clear it?

head: h
Contraindicated
a short list
inv: • newborn kidneys clear it slowly in week 1: slow heart, cyanosis
• same for water-soluble acebutolol, nadolol, sotalol

head: h
Alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, coffee
not contraindicated, except as below
inv: • ≤ 0.5 g/kg (< 2 beers or 1 glass of wine)
risk is infection and sudden infant death, not the milk: not near the baby, change clothes

panels.title: What a drug can do to the fetus
items: miscarriage: mifepristone, misoprostol · growth restriction: beta-blockers, cigarettes
malformation: thalidomide, valproate, isotretinoin, methotrexate · neonatal withdrawal: heroin
neonatal toxicity: chlorpropamide, lithium · neurodevelopment: alcohol, lead, mercury

panels.title: Why keep breastfeeding
items: WHO: breast milk alone for 6 months · the standard of care
↓ diarrhea, pneumonia, otitis media, bronchiolitis · less eczema · ↓ necrotizing enterocolitis · IQ ~+4
look it up: LactMed · Hale's Medications and Mothers' Milk · FRAME
